  gene cluster of Burkholderia lata strain 383. Its amidohydrolase-related fold is compatible with a
  soluble aromatic-ring-cleavage intermediate hydratase. The exact substrate isomer and reaction
  specificity remain unestablished for this protein, including whether it hydrates KCH or an
  oxalomesaconate form.

      ring-cleavage-intermediate role support a cytoplasmic location. This is a
      homology/function-based localization inference, not a fractionation or imaging result in B.
      lata. No more specific localization is asserted.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: file:BURL3/Bcep18194_C7570/Bcep18194_C7570-uniprot.txt
      record_section: ["DR:PANTHER"]
      supporting_text: DR   PANTHER; PTHR21240:SF28; ISO-OROTATE DECARBOXYLASE (EUROFUNG); 1.

  review:

    reason: The amidohydrolase-related fold spans multiple chemical functions. Published cluster
      context supports a LigJ-like hydration hypothesis, which is not hydrolytic bond cleavage. This
      does not experimentally exclude a secondary hydrolytic activity in the unassayed Q39LQ2

description: DesB is a gallate dioxygenase, a homodimeric type II (class III, LigB-family) extradiol ring-cleavage
  dioxygenase in which an N-terminal LigB-like catalytic domain is fused to a C-terminal LigA-like domain,
  so that a single polypeptide corresponds to both subunits of the two-subunit protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase.

  and oxaloacetate by the lower protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway enzymes. The active site contains
  non-heme Fe(II), and substrate binding reorganizes its coordination geometry. In the lignin-degrading
  sphingomonad strain SYK-6, DesB acts in the main route for syringate (syringyl-unit) catabolism, in
  which syringate is O-demethylated via 3-O-methylgallate to gallate before ring cleavage, and it is one
  of two dioxygenases (with LigAB) that degrade gallate. It is functionally equivalent to the GalA gallate
  dioxygenase of gallate-degrading pseudomonads.

document.description: DesB is a gallate dioxygenase, a homodimeric type II (class III, LigB-family) extradiol ring-cleavage dioxygenase in which an N-terminal LigB-like catalytic domain is fused to a C-terminal LigA-like domain, so that a single polypeptide corresponds to both subunits of the two-subunit protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase. It specifically cleaves the aromatic ring of gallate with incorporation of both atoms of O2 to give 4-oxalomesaconate, which is then converted to 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate and cleaved to pyruvate and oxaloacetate by the lower protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway enzymes. It is functionally equivalent to the GalA gallate dioxygenase of gallate-degrading pseudomonads.

description: LigJ is a zinc-dependent hydratase of the amidohydrolase superfamily (distorted

  in the lower protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway that also receives gallate-derived
  4-oxalomesaconate, and thereby in the bacterial catabolism of lignin-derived aromatic compounds.

document.description: LigJ is a zinc-dependent hydratase of the amidohydrolase superfamily (distorted (beta/alpha)8-barrel, cog2159) that catalyses the reversible syn addition of water across the C3=C4 double bond of (3Z)-2-keto-4-carboxy-3-hexenedioate (KCH) to form (4S)-4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate (CHA). The single active-site Zn(2+) polarizes the substrate C2 carbonyl, and Glu-284 acts as general base and then general acid. Originally described as a 4-oxalomesaconate (OMA) hydratase, LigJ acts preferentially on KCH, the product of the LigU 1,3-allylic isomerase, so that in sphingomonads the OMA-to-CHA conversion is carried out by LigU plus LigJ. The homodimeric enzyme is required for growth on vanillate and syringate, functioning in the lower protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway that also receives gallate-derived 4-oxalomesaconate, and thereby in the bacterial catabolism of lignin-derived aromatic compounds.

document.description: LigK is a Mg(2+)-dependent class II pyruvate aldolase of the LigK/PcmE (RraA-like fold) family that catalyses the last step of the protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage (meta-cleavage) pathway: the retro-aldol cleavage of 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate (CHA) to pyruvate and oxaloacetate. id: MODULE:bacterial_gallate_catabolism
title: Bacterial gallate catabolism via 4-oxalomesaconate
description: >-
  A bacterial aromatic-acid catabolic module that opens the gallate ring by
  extradiol dioxygenation and converts the ring-cleavage product to pyruvate and
  oxaloacetate. A two-domain type II extradiol gallate dioxygenase cleaves
  gallate to the keto tautomer of 4-oxalomesaconate (OMA). OMA is then converted
  to 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate (CHA) by one of two enzyme pairs that are
  not homologous at the hydration step: a keto-enol tautomerase plus an OMA-enol
  hydratase of the PIG-L/MshB zinc-hydratase fold, or a 1,3-allylic isomerase
  that forms (3Z)-2-keto-4-carboxy-3-hexenedioate (KCH) plus a KCH hydratase of
  the amidohydrolase fold. A metal-dependent class II CHA aldolase of the
  RraA-like fold finally cleaves CHA to pyruvate and oxaloacetate. An
  outer-membrane porin encoded with the pathway genes can optionally support
  substrate entry. Upstream reactions that generate gallate (for example
  demethylation of syringate-derived 3-O-methylgallate), regulation, and the
  metabolism of the end products are outside the module boundary.
status: COMPLETE
scope: CONCRETE
evidence:
  - source_id: PMID:16030014
    title: Molecular characterization of the gallate dioxygenase from Pseudomonas putida KT2440. The prototype
      of a new subgroup of extradiol dioxygenases.
    statement: >-
      Biochemical and genetic characterization establishes the Fe(II)-dependent
      two-domain gallate dioxygenase GalA as the ring-cleavage enzyme that
      initiates gallate catabolism in Pseudomonas putida.
  - source_id: PMID:21219457
    title: 'Unravelling the gallic acid degradation pathway in bacteria: the gal cluster from Pseudomonas putida.'
    statement: >-
      Genetic and biochemical analysis establishes the GalA, GalD, GalB, and
      GalC reaction sequence from gallate to pyruvate and oxaloacetate and
      reports homologous gal clusters outside the Pseudomonas genus.
  - source_id: PMID:16030198
    title: 'Characterization of the gallate dioxygenase gene: three distinct ring cleavage dioxygenases are involved
      in syringate degradation by Sphingomonas paucimobilis SYK-6.'
    statement: >-
      The sphingomonad gallate dioxygenase DesB, homologous to the LigB/LigA
      protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase subunits as GalA is, converts gallate to
      4-oxalomesaconate, showing that the same ring-cleavage chemistry operates
      in Alphaproteobacteria.
  - source_id: PMID:29658701
    title: Functional Annotation of LigU as a 1,3-Allylic Isomerase during the Degradation of Lignin in the
      Protocatechuate 4,5-Cleavage Pathway from the Soil Bacterium Sphingobium sp. SYK-6.
    statement: >-
      Establishes the sphingomonad LigU isomerase and LigJ hydratase route from
      4-oxalomesaconate through KCH to CHA, the alternative to the GalD/GalB
      route.
  - source_id: PMID:12486039
    title: Characterization of the 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate aldolase gene and operon structure of the
      protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway genes in Sphingomonas paucimobilis SYK-6.
    statement: >-
      Purified LigK, a homolog of GalC, cleaves CHA to pyruvate and
      oxaloacetate and is essential for growth on vanillate and syringate.
  - source_id: PMID:17213657
    title: Genetic and biochemical investigations on bacterial catabolic pathways for lignin-derived aromatic
      compounds.
    statement: Comparative sphingomonad catabolism supports shared lower-pathway context, while the
      Arthrobacter comparison alone does not extend gallate-entry scope.
  - source_id: PMID:31075306
    title: A comparison between the homocyclic aromatic metabolic pathways from plant-derived compounds by
      bacteria and fungi.
    statement: Cross-kingdom review guides comparison but its older intermediate shorthand is superseded by
      the LigU/LigJ mechanistic papers.
  - source_id: PMID:29052962
    title: 'Bacterial catabolism of lignin-derived aromatics: New findings in a recent decade: Update on bacterial
      lignin catabolism.'
    statement: Transport review supports the distinct evidence status of KTGAL GalT, GalP and aromatic-binding
      candidates.
  - source_id: PMID:38064205
    title: 'Bringing up to date the toolkit for the catabolism of aromatic compounds in fungi: The unexpected 1,2,3,5-tetrahydroxybenzene
      central pathway.'
    statement: A distinct fungal tetrahydroxybenzene pathway is a boundary example, not an additional variant
      of the bacterial OMA mechanism.
notes: >-
  Taxonomic scope. The ring-cleavage, CHA-forming, and CHA-cleavage chemistry is characterized in two distantly
  related proteobacterial lineages: the Gammaproteobacterium Pseudomonas putida KT2440 (gal cluster: GalA, GalD,
  GalB, GalC, optional GalP porin) and the sphingomonads Sphingobium (Sphingomonas paucimobilis) SYK-6 and Novosphingobium
  KA1 (DesB, LigU, LigJ, LigK). In SYK-6 these enzymes serve gallate formed from syringate as well as the protocatechuate
  4,5-cleavage pathway, which joins this module at 4-oxalomesaconate. The dioxygenase (NCBIfam NF009904) and CHA
  aldolase (PTHR33254:SF16) steps are homologous between lineages; the keto-enol tautomerase (GO:0016862, EC 5.3.2.8)
  and the C=C-transposing allylic isomerase (GO:0016863, EC 5.3.3.-) are paralogous members of PTHR43709:SF3 with
  different reaction classes; and the two hydratases belong to unrelated folds (PTHR12993 and PTHR21240), which
  is why the OMA-to-CHA segment is a variant set. The modeled scope is Pseudomonadota, the common ancestry of the
  characterized alpha- and gammaproteobacterial pathways and the additional beta-proteobacterial growth evidence.
  Arthrobacter keyseri PcmE supports a shared downstream aldolase, not a gallate-initiated pathway outside this
  phylum. This is an evidence boundary, not an assertion that other bacteria lack gallate catabolism. Homolog presence
  or heterologous complementation alone does not establish an endogenous complete route.
  Boundary. GalP is optional
  because its porin activity and outer-membrane location are supported, but direct gallate specificity and pathway
  essentiality are not. The module begins chemically at gallate and ends at pyruvate plus oxaloacetate. GalR regulation,
  the experimentally characterized KTGAL GalT inner-membrane transporter, the sphingomonad 3-O-methylgallate routes
  (DesZ, LigAB, LigM O-demethylation), and metabolism of the terminal products are adjacent context rather than
  additional core reactions.

  Grounding. Family terms adopt the PANTHER/NCBIfam groundings proposed for this module in the maintainer grounding
  batch (PTHR34596, NCBIfam NF009904, PTHR43709, PTHR12993, PTHR33254), each checked against panther.obo, the PANTHER
  member index, and InterPro (NF009904 matches both GalA Q88JX5 and DesB Q5NTE5). For the isomerase, hydratase and
  aldolase steps the grounding is narrowed to the subfamily that holds the exemplars (PTHR43709:SF3, PTHR12993:SF29,
  PTHR33254:SF16), because the family reviews restrict those activities to those subfamilies. That batch also listed
  the nicotinate-cluster porin NicP (Q88FY7) as a GalP-step representative; it is not adopted because NicP has no
  role in gallate catabolism. PTHR21240:SF28 for LigJ was added from the LigJ UniProt cross-reference and member
  index. PANTHER families are broad (chitoporins, PrpF-like isomerases, PIG-L deacetylases, RraA-like aldolases,
  ACMSD-like amidohydrolases); the module role is carried by the named subfamily members, as recorded in the family
  reviews.

  Chaining. Continuity of each route was manually verified against Rhea: RHEA:28927 (gallate to (1E)-4-oxobut-1-ene-1,2,4-tricarboxylate,
  the OMA keto form), RHEA:28931 (OMA to its enol, 4-carboxy-2-hydroxy-cis,cis-muconate), RHEA:17401 (enol plus
  water to CHA), RHEA:58504 (OMA to KCH), RHEA:58508 (KCH plus water to (2S)-CHA), and RHEA:28935 (CHA to pyruvate
  and oxaloacetate). The derived chaining check is CoA-specific and does not evaluate these intermediates.

  Ontology. Current GO:0047443 includes the CHA-to-oxaloacetate-plus-pyruvate reaction in its definition, although
  its short label emphasizes the HMG substrate. A new CHA activity term is therefore unnecessary; explicit substrate
  and product descriptors disambiguate the reaction. The dated official definition is archived with the GalC review.
  GalD/GalB enol chemistry remains distinct from LigU/LigJ KCH chemistry; older broad OMA terminology must not collapse
  the two variants.


  Additional sampling. BURL3 ring-cleavage and terminal-aldolase representatives extend sampling to Betaproteobacteria.
  The accompanying BURL3 hydratase review is retained as a boundary case: its family placement does not resolve
  KCH versus OMA-enol specificity, so it is not an exact LigJ-step exemplar. No complete BURL3 route is inferred
  from these partial observations.

      The isolated GalP channel substrate spectrum and molecular basis of selectivity remain unresolved.
      Its native uptake contribution and dispensability for growth under the tested conditions are already
      supported.
    boundary: >-
      GalP remains optional. Inner-membrane uptake by KTGAL GalT is known but lies outside this module's
      intracellular chemical boundary.
    gap_kind:
      - BIOLOGY
    status: OPEN
    resolution: >-
      Purified-channel transport and substrate competition measurements would resolve GalP selectivity.
    provenance:
      - reference_id: PMID:29052962
  - gap_statement: >-
      It is not known how the two OMA-to-CHA routes are distributed among
      bacteria carrying gallate dioxygenases, or whether any lineage uses both.
    boundary: >-
      Each route is grounded in one characterized lineage (Pseudomonas gal
      cluster; sphingomonad lig/des genes); route assignment for other
      gallate-degrading taxa is not asserted.
    gap_kind:
      - BIOLOGY
    status: OPEN
    resolution: >-
      Genetic tests of GalD/GalB versus LigU/LigJ homologs in gallate-degrading
      bacteria outside these two lineages, with intermediate detection (OMA
      enol versus KCH), would establish which route each uses.
    provenance:

    title: Genetic and biochemical investigations on bacterial catabolic pathways for lignin-derived aromatic
      compounds.
    reference_review:
      relevance: HIGH
      correctness: VERIFIED
      review_notes: Publisher PDF read; the cached PMID is abstract-only. Review predates the 2018 KCH/LigU

        assignment.
    findings:
      - statement: SYK-6 DesB belongs to the type-II extradiol dioxygenases; its lower catabolic reactions
          converge with protocatechuate degradation.
      - statement: Arthrobacter keyseri has a protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway; this does not establish a
          gallate-specific entry enzyme there.
  - id: PMID:31075306
    title: A comparison between the homocyclic aromatic metabolic pathways from plant-derived compounds by
      bacteria and fungi.
    reference_review:
      relevance: HIGH
      correctness: VERIFIED
      review_notes: Author manuscript retrieved from the University of Helsinki repository. Sections 2.9.2 and
        2.9.5 compare bacteria and fungi. Its intradiol wording for GalA/DesB and its treatment of LigU as an
        OMA tautomerase are not adopted; the mechanistic primary studies resolve both.
    findings:
      - statement: The review places gallate processing in Pseudomonas and sphingomonads alongside proposed
          fungal routes, which require separate enzyme-level evidence.
      - statement: GalC/LigK terminal cleavage produces oxaloacetate and pyruvate; common downstream products
          do not make all ring-opening pathways equivalent.
  - id: PMID:29052962
    title: 'Bacterial catabolism of lignin-derived aromatics: New findings in a recent decade: Update on bacterial
      lignin catabolism.'
    reference_review:
      relevance: HIGH
      correctness: VERIFIED
      review_notes: Full publisher text read, especially transporter table 4 and transport sections; PMID
        cache remains abstract-only. Supports transport boundaries rather than a new assignment of catalytic
        chemistry.
    findings:
      - statement: GalT has experimental transport support in the adapted KTGAL strain; aromatic-binding
          proteins and predicted transporters elsewhere are not equivalent evidence.
      - statement: The review separates porins, substrate-specific channels and inner-membrane transport
          systems.

    title: 'Bringing up to date the toolkit for the catabolism of aromatic compounds in fungi: The unexpected 1,2,3,5-tetrahydroxybenzene
      central pathway.'
    reference_review:
      relevance: HIGH
      correctness: VERIFIED
      review_notes: Full cached primary paper inspected; comparative fungal boundary evidence, not a bacterial
        exemplar.
    findings:
      - statement: Aspergillus gallate use can proceed through a distinct tetrahydroxybenzene pathway, so
          gallate utilization alone does not identify the bacterial OMA mechanism.
  - id: PMID:21219457
    title: 'Unravelling the gallic acid degradation pathway in bacteria: the gal cluster from Pseudomonas putida.'
    reference_review:
      relevance: HIGH
      correctness: VERIFIED
      review_notes: Full publisher text read separately from the protected abstract-only cache. Distinguish
        the adapted KTGAL strain from its KT2440 parent; native growth, heterologous complementation and
        enzyme assays have different scopes.
    findings:
      - statement: KTGAL restores a frameshifted GalT transporter; GalP disruption reduces uptake without
          abolishing growth.

document.title: Bacterial gallate catabolism via 4-oxalomesaconate
document.description: A bacterial aromatic-acid catabolic module that opens the gallate ring by extradiol dioxygenation and converts the ring-cleavage product to pyruvate and oxaloacetate. A two-domain type II extradiol gallate dioxygenase cleaves gallate to the keto tautomer of 4-oxalomesaconate (OMA). OMA is then converted to 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate (CHA) by one of two enzyme pairs that are not homologous at the hydration step: a keto-enol tautomerase plus an OMA-enol hydratase of the PIG-L/MshB zinc-hydratase fold, or a 1,3-allylic isomerase that forms (3Z)-2-keto-4-carboxy-3-hexenedioate (KCH) plus a KCH hydratase of the amidohydrolase fold. A metal-dependent class II CHA aldolase of the RraA-like fold finally cleaves CHA to pyruvate and oxaloacetate. An outer-membrane porin encoded with the pathway genes can optionally support substrate entry. Upstream reactions that generate gallate (for example demethylation of syringate-derived 3-O-methylgallate), regulation, and the metabolism of the end products are outside the module boundary.

document.notes:
Taxonomic scope. The ring-cleavage, CHA-forming, and CHA-cleavage chemistry is characterized in two distantly related proteobacterial lineages: the Gammaproteobacterium Pseudomonas putida KT2440 (gal cluster: GalA, GalD, GalB, GalC, optional GalP porin) and the sphingomonads Sphingobium (Sphingomonas paucimobilis) SYK-6 and Novosphingobium KA1 (DesB, LigU, LigJ, LigK). In SYK-6 these enzymes serve gallate formed from syringate as well as the protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage pathway, which joins this module at 4-oxalomesaconate. The dioxygenase (NCBIfam NF009904) and CHA aldolase (PTHR33254:SF16) steps are homologous between lineages; the keto-enol tautomerase (GO:0016862, EC 5.3.2.8) and the C=C-transposing allylic isomerase (GO:0016863, EC 5.3.3.-) are paralogous members of PTHR43709:SF3 with different reaction classes; and the two hydratases belong to unrelated folds (PTHR12993 and PTHR21240), which is why the OMA-to-CHA segment is a variant set. The modeled scope is Pseudomonadota, the common ancestry of the characterized alpha- and gammaproteobacterial pathways and the additional beta-proteobacterial growth evidence. Arthrobacter keyseri PcmE supports a shared downstream aldolase, not a gallate-initiated pathway outside this phylum. This is an evidence boundary, not an assertion that other bacteria lack gallate catabolism. Homolog presence or heterologous complementation alone does not establish an endogenous complete route. Boundary. GalP is optional because its porin activity and outer-membrane location are supported, but direct gallate specificity and pathway essentiality are not. The module begins chemically at gallate and ends at pyruvate plus oxaloacetate. GalR regulation, the experimentally characterized KTGAL GalT inner-membrane transporter, the sphingomonad 3-O-methylgallate routes (DesZ, LigAB, LigM O-demethylation), and metabolism of the terminal products are adjacent context rather than additional core reactions.
Grounding. Family terms adopt the PANTHER/NCBIfam groundings proposed for this module in the maintainer grounding batch (PTHR34596, NCBIfam NF009904, PTHR43709, PTHR12993, PTHR33254), each checked against panther.obo, the PANTHER member index, and InterPro (NF009904 matches both GalA Q88JX5 and DesB Q5NTE5). For the isomerase, hydratase and aldolase steps the grounding is narrowed to the subfamily that holds the exemplars (PTHR43709:SF3, PTHR12993:SF29, PTHR33254:SF16), because the family reviews restrict those activities to those subfamilies. That batch also listed the nicotinate-cluster porin NicP (Q88FY7) as a GalP-step representative; it is not adopted because NicP has no role in gallate catabolism. PTHR21240:SF28 for LigJ was added from the LigJ UniProt cross-reference and member index. PANTHER families are broad (chitoporins, PrpF-like isomerases, PIG-L deacetylases, RraA-like aldolases, ACMSD-like amidohydrolases); the module role is carried by the named subfamily members, as recorded in the family reviews.
Chaining. Continuity of each route was manually verified against Rhea: RHEA:28927 (gallate to (1E)-4-oxobut-1-ene-1,2,4-tricarboxylate, the OMA keto form), RHEA:28931 (OMA to its enol, 4-carboxy-2-hydroxy-cis,cis-muconate), RHEA:17401 (enol plus water to CHA), RHEA:58504 (OMA to KCH), RHEA:58508 (KCH plus water to (2S)-CHA), and RHEA:28935 (CHA to pyruvate and oxaloacetate). The derived chaining check is CoA-specific and does not evaluate these intermediates.
Ontology. Current GO:0047443 includes the CHA-to-oxaloacetate-plus-pyruvate reaction in its definition, although its short label emphasizes the HMG substrate. A new CHA activity term is therefore unnecessary; explicit substrate and product descriptors disambiguate the reaction. The dated official definition is archived with the GalC review. GalD/GalB enol chemistry remains distinct from LigU/LigJ KCH chemistry; older broad OMA terminology must not collapse the two variants.

Additional sampling. BURL3 ring-cleavage and terminal-aldolase representatives extend sampling to Betaproteobacteria. The accompanying BURL3 hydratase review is retained as a boundary case: its family placement does not resolve KCH versus OMA-enol specificity, so it is not an exact LigJ-step exemplar. No complete BURL3 route is inferred from these partial observations.

Recombinant GalB directly hydrates OMAenol/CHM to CHA, contains one zinc per subunit and forms a homohexamer (PMID:21219457, full publisher text read). # ligK (G2IQQ8, Sphingobium sp. SYK-6) - curator notes

Deep research could not be run for this session; these notes were written by hand from the
cached publications and the UniProt record. No `-deep-research-*.md` file exists.

## Identity
- LigK = 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate (CHA) aldolase / oxaloacetate decarboxylase,
  228 aa, LigK/PcmE family (TIGR02798; RraA-like fold, PF03737). PANTHER PTHR33254:SF16,
  the same subfamily as P. putida GalC (genes/PSEPK/galC).
- Strain name history: SYK-6 was originally *Sphingomonas paucimobilis* SYK-6, now
  *Sphingobium* sp. SYK-6.

## Function (experimental)
- CHA aldolase: [PMID:12486039 "This result indicated that LigK catalyzes the conversion of CHA to pyruvate and oxaloacetate."]
- Oxaloacetate decarboxylase (secondary): [PMID:12486039 "It is concluded that LigK is able to decarboxylate oxaloacetate to generate pyruvate."]
  The CHA reaction is much faster: [PMID:12486039 "The V max for CHA aldol cleavage (265 U/mg) is 20 times higher than that for oxaloacetate decarboxylation (13.2 U/mg)."]
- Metal dependence / class II aldolase: [PMID:12486039 "LigK was suggested to be one of the class II aldolases, which require the metal ion."]
- Oligomer: [PMID:12486039 "This result suggested that LigK is a homohexamer."]
- Product inhibition: [PMID:12486039 "CHA aldolase activity was inhibited by oxaloacetate with a K i value of 23 μM."]
- HMG formation from 2 pyruvate is attributed by UniProt to PMID:29658701 (abstract-only in cache; abstract does not mention LigK)
  [file:SPHSK/ligK/ligK-uniprot.txt "Is also able to catalyze the formation of 4-hydroxy-4-methyl-2-oxoglutarate (HMG) from two molecules of pyruvate"].

## Pathway role
- Terminal step of the PCA 4,5-cleavage pathway: [PMID:12486039 "Finally, CHA is cleaved by CHA aldolase to produce pyruvate and oxaloacetate."]
- Essential in vivo: [PMID:12486039 "The obtained mutant strain DLK completely lost the ability to grow on both vanillate and syringate."]
- Syringate-derived carbon (3-O-methylgallate, gallate) converges on OMA:
  [PMID:12486039 "In this alternative pathway, 3MGA was finally converted to OMA and then entered the PCA 4,5-cleavage pathway."]
  and DesB converts gallate to OMA [PMID:16030198 "DesB specifically attacked gallate to generate 4-oxalomesaconate as the reaction product."]
  Hence LigK also performs the last step of gallate catabolism in this organism (NEW GO:0019396),
  matching GalC's GO:0019396 in P. putida.
- Upstream sphingomonad route OMA -> KCH (LigU) -> CHA (LigJ):
  [PMID:29658701 "LigJ catalyzes the hydration of KCH to 4-carboxy-4-hydroxy-2-oxoadipate."]

## Curation decisions
- GO:0047443 (HMG aldolase; definition includes the CHA reaction) = core MF, ACCEPT all three rows.
- GO:0008948 oxaloacetate decarboxylase = real but secondary -> KEEP_AS_NON_CORE (both rows).
- GO:0019617 PCA meta-cleavage IDA = ACCEPT (core BP).
- GO:0046274 lignin catabolic process (UniPathway IEA) = KEEP_AS_NON_CORE (acts on lignin-monomer-derived
  intermediates, not the polymer).
- Proposed CHA-specific aldolase term (same proposed_name as galC review).


## 2026-11-06 comparative source and annotation audit

PMID:12486039 full text directly identifies CHA→pyruvate+oxaloacetate by ESI-MS, secondary oxaloacetate decarboxylation, magnesium dependence, and a homohexamer. Current GO:0047443 includes CHA cleavage explicitly; the short HMG name is not evidence of a different target reaction. Retain directly demonstrated secondary OAA decarboxylase as non-core. HMG formation is curated from PMID:29658701, whose protected cache is abstract-only; do not invent its assay conditions. Retain historical gallate NEW and the PCA pathway assertion. Replace polymer-level lignin scope with the chemically defined lower PCA pathway.

# Gallate catabolism audit — 2026-11-06

The audit covers gallate ring cleavage, the two chemically distinct OMA-to-CHA routes, terminal CHA cleavage and optional GalP entry. It does not equate growth on gallate with a particular enzyme set, or a shared lower-pathway enzyme with an entire native pathway.

## Comparative literature and scope

Three reviews were searched and read: Masai et al. 2007 ([PMID:17213657](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17213657/)), Kamimura et al. 2017 ([PMID:29052962](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29052962/)), and Lubbers et al. 2019 ([PMID:31075306](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31075306/)). The first publisher PDF and the third author manuscript have independently retrieved text and provenance in the module source-analysis directory. The second was read on the publisher website; its cached PMID remains abstract-only. Module references record individual findings and the limits of each source.

The 2007 synthesis connects the sphingomonad lower pathway to protocatechuate catabolism and describes analogous downstream machinery in Arthrobacter. That comparison supports component homology, not gallate-specific entry outside Pseudomonadota. The model now uses Pseudomonadota as its evidence-backed taxon scope, without making a biological absence claim for other bacteria.

The 2019 comparison is useful for locating fungal alternatives, but two descriptions are unsuitable as mechanistic specifications: it calls GalA/DesB cleavage intradiol and groups LigU with keto-enol tautomerases. The primary studies distinguish extradiol cleavage and the LigU allylic reaction. The 2024 Aspergillus study ([PMID:38064205](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38064205/)) supports a distinct tetrahydroxybenzene route; fungal gallate use alone therefore does not justify adding fungal exemplars here.

## Reactions and family boundaries

Every catalytic leaf carries primary evidence. GalD/GalB and LigU/LigJ remain paired alternatives because their immediate intermediates differ. Broad fold or enzyme-class matches cannot substitute for substrate-specific evidence. GalD and LigU share the PrpF-related family; GalB and LigJ use unrelated folds. The current GO:0047443 definition already covers CHA cleavage, so the archived GalC term proposal is redundant. Its short HMG-based label does not change that definition.

GalB's retained GO:0047584 has keto-OMA wording, whereas its measured immediate substrate is OMA-enol. The curated Rhea reaction and explicit chemical descriptors preserve the distinction. No gene source annotation was rewritten to conceal that ontology mismatch.

The KA1 LigU exemplar is supported directly by [PMID:31339729](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31339729/), whose abstract identifies the organism. A SYK-6-focused paper title was insufficient reason to reject the target assignment. A collection of enzyme exemplars across strains is not proof that one strain expresses the whole modeled route.

## Sampling and evidence limits

Nine inherited reviews span Pseudomonas, Sphingobium and Novosphingobium. Three seeded Burkholderia lata 383 reviews extend the audit to a beta-proteobacterial strain with reported native gallate utilization. The ring-cleavage and terminal-aldolase representatives have the declared family signatures independently of submitter/ARBA function names. The hydratase remains a reviewed boundary candidate because its precise KCH versus OMA-enol activity is unresolved. These partial assignments do not establish a complete molecular route in BURL3.

Transport interpretation distinguishes the adapted KTGAL strain from parental KT2440. The known GalT transporter is adjacent to the chemical module boundary, not an unidentified candidate. GalP contributes to native uptake, but isolated-channel selectivity remains an experimental question. The 2017 transporter review supports this separation.

## Verification in progress

The nine existing reviews preserve 50 annotation payloads, including nine inherited NEW rows. No annotation was added or retired in that panel. The new BURL3 panel has ten seeded rows. Exact source and provider preservation, focused validations and generated histories are recorded in the consultation manifests. The rebuilt family index confirms the declared representatives. All 24 production coverage and boundary cases pass; the chemical oracle and its limits are explicit. Three module conformance advisories concern specific proposed core terms, not missing chemistry. Whole-repository validation and a dedicated PR remain pending.
